text: # Global University AI Policy Audit 2026 > **Atlanta College of Liberal Arts and Sciences (ACLAS)** — published as part of [Study Intelligence](https://aclas.si), the university's open research program · [aclas.college](https://aclas.college) An open dataset of **186 audit records** covering whether universities publish official guidance on student/staff use of generative AI. Compiled 2026-10-14 by Study Intelligence (aclas.si) as research for *The Second Printing Press: Higher Education for the Intelligence Age*. > **Also on Kaggle:** [aclascollege/ai-policy-audit-2026](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/aclascollege/ai-policy-audit-2026) — download the CSV without git, or fork it straight into a notebook. ## In plain English **What is this?** A spreadsheet answering one question for 186 universities worldwide: *does this school officially tell students and staff how they're allowed to use AI (like ChatGPT)?* We checked each university's own website, page by page.

**Why does it matter?** If you're a student, it tells you whether your school has clear AI rules or is making it up as it goes. If you're a teacher or policymaker, it shows the global norm: almost nobody bans AI outright — instead, teachers set the rules per course and students must disclose AI use. **The one chart that matters:** Rich universities are far more likely to have AI rules (92% of the top 50) than universities in the Global South (46%). The AI policy gap *is* the wealth gap. ## Try it (30 seconds) ## FAQ **I'm a journalist. What's the headline?** "Not one of the world's top-100 universities bans AI campus-wide. The debate about banning AI on campus is, empirically, over." **I'm a student. How do I use this?** Find your school's row, open the `policy_url`, and read what it actually allows. Rules differ wildly.

**Can I trust a single row?** It's a snapshot from 2026-10-14 — policies change. 15 schools appear twice (flagged `name_overlap`); rows marked `UNCLEAR` mean "we couldn't verify", not "no policy". **How do I cite it?** See `CITATION.cff`, or: Atlanta College of Liberal Arts and Sciences (ACLAS) — Study Intelligence (aclas.si), 2026, CC-BY-4.0. ## Headline numbers | Sample | Rows | Published AI policy (YES) | No policy (NO) | Unclear | |---|---|---|---|---| | QS 2026 ranks 1–50 | 50 | 46 (92%) | 1 | 3 | | QS 2026 ranks 51–100 | 49 | 43 | 0 | 6 | | QS 2026 ranks 101–150 | 50 | 38 | 6 | 6 | | Global South flagships | 37 | 17 (46%) | 17 | 3 | | **Total** | **186** | **144 (77%)** | **24** | **18** |

Key finding: **not one of the top-100 universities imposes a campus-wide AI ban.** The global norm is delegated permission — instructors set per-course AI rules, students disclose AI use. The policy gap maps onto the wealth gap: 92% of the top 50 publish guidance vs 46% of Global South flagships. ## Files | File | Format | Description | |---|---|---| | `ai-policy-audit-2026.csv` | CSV (UTF-8) | 186 rows, 14 columns | | `ai-policy-audit-2026.json` | JSON | Same data + dataset metadata | | `METHODOLOGY.md` | Markdown | How the audit was conducted, definitions, caveats | | `parse.py` | Python 3 | The exact script that generated CSV/JSON from the raw audit tables | | `CITATION.cff` | CFF | Machine-readable citation | ## Columns

| Column | Description | |---|---| | `id` | Stable row id, e.g. `qs-14`, `gs-10` (`-2` suffix where QS ranks tie) | | `sample` | `qs_top_50` / `qs_51_100` / `qs_101_150` / `global_south` | | `rank` | QS 2026 rank as printed in source (`=17` = tied rank); null for Global South | | `university` | Institution name | | `country` | Country (Global South sample only) | | `official_domain` | University's official domain (QS samples only) | | `has_policy` | `YES` / `NO` / `UNCLEAR` | | `policy_url` | First URL found in the source cell (null when none) | | `policy_url_raw` | Original cell text when it contained more than just the URL | | `page_title` | Title of the policy page | | `date_info` | Date / last-updated as shown on the page (often "Not shown") | | `scope` | Who the policy covers, e.g. `student-facing / exams-integrity` | | `note` | Auditor's one-line note | | `name_overlap` | `true` for the 30 rows (15 universities) audited in more than one sample | ## Honest notes on the numbers

- The published summary said "187 universities". The source tables contain **186 data rows** covering **171 unique university names** — 15 names appear in two samples (the rank-band files overlap: e.g. TU Delft at QS 47 and QS 61). Rows are kept as audited; `name_overlap` flags them. Deduplicate on `university` if you need institution-level counts. - `UNCLEAR` (18) means "could not verify", not "confirmed absent" — dead links, portal-gated intranets and non-English sites are the main causes. True adoption is likely higher than 77%. - ~5 of the Global South YES cases are faculty/school-level rather than university-wide. - Snapshot date: **2026-10-14**. Policies are being published monthly; treat as a snapshot, not a live registry. Contributions and corrections welcome via issues/PRs. ## License [CC-BY-4.0](LICENSE) — use it, build on it, just cite it. ## Citation See `CITATION.cff` for the machine-readable version.

# Methodology — Global University AI Policy Audit 2026 Audit date: **2026-10-14**. Snapshot, not a live registry. ## What was counted **YES** = a page on the university's **own official domain** containing guidance or policy on AI use (students, teaching, research, or all-community). Generic academic-integrity pages that never mention AI do **not** count. **NO** = searched in English (+ local language for non-English countries) and found no such page. **UNCLEAR** = could not verify — dead links, portal-gated intranets, crawler-blocked domains (e.g. ui.ac.id), or insufficient evidence either way. ## How each record was verified Web search + direct verification: each policy URL below was opened and confirmed to load AI usage guidance on 2026-10-14, or corroborated by search-engine crawl of the official page plus the MDPI April 2026 systematic audit of top-200 universities' GenAI guidelines where direct fetch failed.

Searches ran in English + local languages (German, French, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, Portuguese, Arabic, Indonesian, Thai, Vietnamese). This matters: continental European and East Asian universities often publish first in the national language, and English-only surveys systematically undercount them. ## Samples - **QS 2026 ranks 1–50** (50 rows), **51–100** (49 rows), **101–150** (50 rows): every ranked institution checked in order. - **Global South flagships** (37 rows): flagship universities across Brazil, Argentina, Egypt, Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Mexico, Chile, China. ## Known limitations (read before citing)

1. 15 university names appear in two samples (30 rows flagged `name_overlap`) — the rank-band files overlap (e.g. TU Delft listed at QS 47 and QS 61). Institution-level counts should deduplicate on `university`. 2. ~5 Global South YES cases are faculty/school-level, not university-wide. 3. Last-updated dates are inconsistently displayed by universities; "issued in the last 12 months" is approximate. 4. Two secondary-literature errors were caught and excluded during the audit (a paper conflating Quinnipiac's catalog with Qatar University; a micro-credential page cited as a "policy"). 5. Policies are being published monthly — verify before citing any single row for a current claim. ## Reproducibility `parse.py` in this directory is the exact script that generated the CSV/JSON from the raw audit tables. Raw tables: `~/workspace/aclas-report/ai-policy-audit/` (`qs-001-050.md`, `qs-051-100.md`, `qs-101-150.md`, `global-south-35.md`). Corrections welcome via issues or pull requests.

# Central Asia AI Education Audit 2026 > **Atlanta College of Liberal Arts and Sciences (ACLAS)** — published as part of [Study Intelligence](https://aclas.si), the university's open research program · [aclas.college](https://aclas.college) An open dataset of **31 leading universities across Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan**, audited on two questions: (a) does it publish a public, university-level AI usage policy? (b) what AI-related degree programs or courses does it offer? > **Also on Kaggle:** [aclascollege/central-asia-ai-education-audit-2026](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/aclascollege/central-asia-ai-education-audit-2026) — download the CSV without git, or fork it straight into a notebook. ## In plain English **What is this?** A report card for 31 leading universities in Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan on two questions: *do they publish AI rules?* and *do they teach AI?* **The headline:**

Schools are teaching AI **three times faster** than they're writing rules for it (58% offer AI programs vs 19% with a policy). And four of the six schools *with* policies are in Kazakhstan — Turkmenistan and Tajikistan are near-complete blind spots. ## Try it (30 seconds) ## FAQ **Why Central Asia?** It's the least-measured region in global AI-education research. English-only surveys systematically miss it — this audit searched in Russian and local languages too. **What does UNVERIFIABLE mean?** We couldn't confirm a policy on the public web — often because sites are down, login-walled, or crawler-blocked. It's a finding about *transparency*, not just adoption. ## Headline numbers

- **6 of 31 (19%)** publish a verifiable public AI usage policy on their official domain — 4 of the 6 are Kazakh, backed by a 2024 inter-university AI standard and a 2025 ministry position against AI bans. - **18 of 31 (58%)** offer a verifiable AI-named degree program or AI course portfolio — institutions are teaching AI ~3× faster than they govern its use. - **Zero** campus-wide AI bans. Every verified policy follows the global norm of *delegated permission plus mandatory disclosure*. - **Turkmenistan and Tajikistan are near-complete blind spots:** 0 of 7 sampled universities publish a verifiable policy. - The **UNVERIFIABLE rate (81%) is the highest of any region measured** — a finding about transparency and discoverability as much as about adoption. ## Files

| File | Description | |---|---| | `central-asia-ai-policies-2026.csv` / `.json` | 31 rows: AI policy per university | | `central-asia-ai-programs-2026.csv` | 31 rows: verified AI programs/courses per university | | `central-asia-ai-education-audit-2026.json` | Both tables + metadata | | `METHODOLOGY.md` | Sample selection, definitions, caveats | | `parse.py` | Exact script that generated CSV/JSON from the raw audit tables | ## Columns — policies `id`, `country_code` (KZ/KG/UZ/TJ/TM), `university`, `has_policy` (`YES`/`UNVERIFIABLE` — no confirmed-NO cases in this sample; unverifiable means not found, not proven absent), `policy_url`, `policy_url_raw`, `note`. ## Columns — programs `id`, `university`, `ai_programs` (verified AI-named programs/courses), `source_url`, `source_url_raw`. ## Notes

- Snapshot date: **2026-10-17**. QAIRU (Qazaq AI Research University, Central Asia's first purpose-built AI university) enrolled its first 528 students in September 2026 — included where verifiable. - Corrections welcome via issues/PRs. ## License [CC-BY-4.0](LICENSE) — cite "Atlanta College of Liberal Arts and Sciences (ACLAS) — Study Intelligence (aclas.si)". --- Published by the **Atlanta College of Liberal Arts and Sciences (ACLAS)** as part of [Study Intelligence](https://aclas.si), an open research program on AI and higher education. ## Citation

# Online Degree Tuition 2026 > **Atlanta College of Liberal Arts and Sciences (ACLAS)** — published as part of [Study Intelligence](https://aclas.si), the university's open research program · [aclas.college](https://aclas.college) An open dataset of **740 online degree programs at 537 U.S. institutions**, with tuition verified against each university's official website. Built for the cheapest-online-degrees tool (aclas.edu.gr) and released here as open data. > **Also on Kaggle:** [aclascollege/online-degree-tuition-2026](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/aclascollege/online-degree-tuition-2026) — download the CSV without git, or fork it straight into a notebook. ## In plain English **What is this?** The price tag for 740 online degrees at 537 US schools — every number checked against the university's own official website. If you've ever wondered "what does an online MBA *actually* cost?", this is the answer, in a spreadsheet. **The picture:**

A master's in computer science (median $26k) costs roughly *half* a bachelor's (median $50k). Online MBAs cluster around $27k — far below the six-figure sticker prices that dominate headlines. ## Try it (30 seconds) ## FAQ **I'm shopping for a degree. How do I use this?** Filter by `level`, sort by `tuition_usd`, and open `source_url` to verify the price is current before you apply. Prices change; this is a snapshot from 2026-10-15. **What does `estimate: true` mean?** The school only publishes per-credit prices, so we multiplied by required credits. Treat it as a comparison, not a quote — the math is shown in `tuition_note`. **Why is this free?** It's open data (CC-BY-4.0). Cite "Atlanta College of Liberal Arts and Sciences (ACLAS) — Study Intelligence (aclas.si)". ## Coverage | Level | Programs | |---|---| | Online MBA | 228 | | Online DBA | 38 | | Business bachelor's | 299 | | Online BSCS | 67 | | Online MCS | 108 | | **Total** | **740** | ## Columns

`school`, `program`, `level` (mba/dba/bachelor/bscs/mcs), `tuition_usd` (total program tuition in USD), `tuition_note`, `estimate` (true = figure is an informed estimate, e.g. per-credit × required credits — see note below), `accreditation`, `format`, `source_url` (the official page the figure was taken from), `verified` (date last checked, 2026-10-15), `operator_owned` (TRUE = program is operated by ACLAS itself, the publisher of this dataset). ## Honest notes

- `estimate: true` (587 rows, 79%) means the total is computed, not quoted — e.g. per-credit-hour price × program credits. The `tuition_note` explains the basis. Treat these as comparisons, not quotes. - **Disclosure:** 5 rows (`operator_owned: TRUE`) are programs operated by ACLAS itself — MBA $89, BBA $159, DBA $199, BSCS $199, MCS $299, sourced from aclas.edu.gr. They are included because the prices are real and verifiable, and flagged so you can exclude them from your own analysis. If you cite "cheapest in category" from this dataset, disclose this too. - Tuition changes; `verified` tells you how fresh each row is. Verify before citing a single figure for a current claim. - USD conversions use the rate at time of verification. ## License [CC-BY-4.0](LICENSE) — cite "Atlanta College of Liberal Arts and Sciences (ACLAS) — Study Intelligence (aclas.si)".

# Methodology — US Carnegie R1 AI Policy Audit 2026 Audit date: **2026-10-17**. Snapshot, not a live registry. ## Universe All **187 institutions** in the 2025 Carnegie Classification R1 category ("very high research activity"), cross-checked against the Wikipedia "List of research universities in the United States" R1 table re-fetched on audit day: exact match, 0 missing / 0 extra. (The "146" figure sometimes cited is the 2021 Carnegie count.) ## What counts Same rules as the global audit (`../ai-policy-audit-2026/METHODOLOGY.md`):

- **YES** = a page on the university's **own official domain** containing guidance/policy on AI use (students, teaching, research, or all-community). Every YES URL was opened and confirmed live on 2026-10-17 (crawl-corroboration fallback transparently noted where used). - **NO** = adopted no AI policy after real searching (English). - **UNCLEAR** = could not verify (rate-blocked, portal-gated, third-party domain only, draft-only). Highest-risk: CUNY Graduate Center ("Draft" label), Kansas / Kansas State (guidance but "no university-wide policy" stated), WVU / WPI / Yale (crawl-only), MUSC (policy NetID-gated). - Two rows were corrected during the audit; provenance kept in `raw/us-r1-batch-10-fix.md` and `raw/us-r1-batch-13-fix.md`. ## Reproducibility `parse.py` generated CSV/JSON from `raw/` batch tables (fixes applied).

# AUDIT LOG — US Carnegie R1 AI Policy Audit (2026-10-17) Auditor: Study Intelligence (aclas.si research). Audit date: **2026-10-17**. Methodology: `~/workspace/study-intelligence/datasets/ai-policy-audit-2026/METHODOLOGY.md` (same as the 187-school global audit) — English search, YES only when a page on the university's OWN official domain contains AI usage guidance/policy; NO only after real searching; UNCLEAR when unverifiable (dead links, portal-gated, rate-limited, etc.). A wrong YES is worse than an UNCLEAR. Raw tables: `raw/us-r1-batch-1.md` … `raw/us-r1-batch-16.md` (15 batches × 12 schools + final batch × 7 schools = 187 rows). ## R1 list source + coverage check

# Online Institutions Across Academic Databases 2026 > **Atlanta College of Liberal Arts and Sciences (ACLAS)** — published as part of [Study Intelligence](https://aclas.si), the university's open research program · [aclas.college](https://aclas.college) [ ](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23445888) [ ](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/aclascollege/academic-database-recognition-2026) [ ](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ACLASCollege/academic-database-recognition-2026) When a new online institution appears, which academic infrastructure databases recognize it — and how quickly? This audit checks **35 institutions** (stratified sample) against **4 academic databases**, documenting each database's inclusion bar. > **Also on Kaggle:** [aclascollege/academic-database-recognition-2026](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/aclascollege/academic-database-recognition-2026) — download the CSV without git, or fork it straight into a notebook. ## In plain English

**What is this?** A spreadsheet answering one question for 35 institutions: *which academic databases recognize this school?* We checked each institution against 4 databases — swot (JetBrains domain list), Wikidata, ROR, and OpenAlex — and recorded who says "yes". **Why does it matter?** New online universities face a "recognition ladder": they get listed first by community databases, then by curated ones. If you're evaluating an unfamiliar school, this shows you where it stands on that ladder — and how far it still has to climb. ## Headline findings

- **Databases discriminate**: traditional elites average **2.8/4**, established online universities **2.6/4**, new alternatives **1.7/4**, documented diploma mills **0.8/4**. - **There is a recognition ladder**: new institutions are typically recognized first by swot (JetBrains, community-reviewed domain list — lowest barrier), then Wikidata (notability), then ROR (curated), then OpenAlex (ingests ROR upstream). - **ACLAS** (Atlanta College of Liberal Arts and Sciences) is on the **first rung**: recognized by JetBrains swot in October 2026 — ahead of EU-accredited Woolf University (founded 2018, 0/4) and Ubiquity University (0/4). ROR application in progress; OpenAlex follows ROR ingestion. - **Wikidata nuance**: 8 of 10 controversial institutions have Wikidata entries — documenting them *as frauds* (DOJ cases, AG suits). Wikidata presence signals notability, not legitimacy. - **Global census (v2)**: of 16,822 universities worldwide (Wikidata frame), 41% score 4/4, 34% score 3/4, 7% sc

ore 2/4, 18% score 1/4. swot domain coverage: 47% globally (US 68%, India 21%). ## Try it (30 seconds) ## Files - `academic-database-recognition-2026.csv` — **v1 curated panel**: one row per institution: `id, name, country, tier, founded, website, domain`, per-database `in_swot / in_ror / in_openalex / in_wikidata` (0/1) with `*_id` / evidence URLs, `recognition_score` (n/4), `checked_date`, `notes`. - `global-recognition-census-2026.csv` — **v2 global census**: 16,822 universities worldwide (Wikidata frame) with `in_wikidata` (=1, frame), `in_ror` (Wikidata-recorded ROR ID, ~5% false-negative rate), `in_swot` (exact domain match, 26,914 swot domains), `in_openalex` (ROR-ID lookup via OpenAlex API; NULL if no ROR ID). - `METHODOLOGY.md` — audit method, tier definitions, matching rules, caveats. - `check.py` — verification script used during the audit. - `CITATION.cff` — machine-readable citation. ## Tiers

- **A** — established online/distance universities (n=10) - **B** — new / alternative institutions (n=10) - **C** — controversial institutions, as contrast (n=10) - **D** — traditional elite baseline, methodology validation (n=5) ## Limitations - Exact-name matching is conservative: variant names may be missed (false negatives possible). - Snapshot 2026-10-18; databases update on their own cycles. - swot checks the registered domain; institutions without a known domain are marked absent there. - The v2 census builds on the Wikidata frame: institutions missing from Wikidata are missing from v2 by construction. ## Citation Atlanta College of Liberal Arts and Sciences (ACLAS) — Study Intelligence. *Online Institutions Across Academic Databases 2026* (v1.0.0, 2026-10-18). # Online Institutions Across Academic Databases 2026 > Open dataset: 35 institutions checked against 4 academic infrastructure > databases (swot, Wikidata, ROR, OpenAlex) plus a 16,822-university global > census. By Study Intelligence, Atlanta College of Liberal Arts and Sciences > (ACLAS) (https://aclas.si). > License: CC-BY-4.0. Snapshot: 2026-10-18. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23445888. ## What question does this answer? When a new online institution appears, which academic infrastructure databases recognize it — and how quickly? Each of the 35 v1 institutions was checked directly against each database's own record system; the v2 census joins Wikidata, ROR, OpenAlex and swot at global scale. ## Key findings

- Recognition forms a ladder: swot (community-reviewed domains, lowest bar) → Wikidata (notability) → ROR (curated) → OpenAlex (ingests ROR upstream). - Traditional elites average 2.8/4 databases, established online universities 2.6/4, new alternatives 1.7/4, documented diploma mills 0.8/4. - ACLAS sits on the first rung (swot-recognized, Oct 2026), ahead of EU-accredited Woolf University (founded 2018, 0/4). - Wikidata presence signals notability, not legitimacy: 8 of 10 controversial institutions have entries documenting them *as frauds*. - Global census: 41% of 16,822 universities score 4/4; swot domain coverage is 47% globally (US 68%, India 21%). ## Files

- `academic-database-recognition-2026.csv` — v1 curated panel: 35 rows, per-database 0/1 flags with ids and evidence URLs, recognition_score (n/4), checked_date, notes - `global-recognition-census-2026.csv` — v2 global census: 16,822 rows (Wikidata frame) with in_wikidata / in_ror / in_swot / in_openalex - `METHODOLOGY.md` — audit method, tier definitions, matching rules, caveats - `check.py` — verification script used during the audit - `CITATION.cff` — machine-readable citation ## Columns (v1 CSV) `id`, `name`, `country`, `tier` (A/B/C/D), `founded`, `website`, `domain`, `in_swot` / `in_ror` / `in_openalex` / `in_wikidata` (0/1) with `*_id` and evidence URLs, `recognition_score` (n/4), `checked_date`, `notes`. ## Caveats

- Exact-name matching is conservative: variant names may be missed (false negatives possible). - v2 builds on the Wikidata frame; institutions missing from Wikidata are missing from v2 by construction. ~5% false-negative rate on ROR via Wikidata-recorded ids. - Snapshot 2026-10-18; databases update on their own cycles. ## Citation Study Intelligence (https://aclas.si).
